name: Earth and Moon: mission design (J2000.0)
description: Earth and the Moon as point masses about their common barycentre (no Sun), initial states from JPL Horizons at J2000.0. A mission-design sandbox: add a spacecraft, plan a transfer to the Moon and fly it. Contacts stop the simulation.
frame: Ecliptic and mean equinox of J2000.0 (Horizons REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, REF_SYSTEM=ICRF); right-handed; the x-y plane is the ecliptic
origin: Barycentre of Earth and the Moon (zero total momentum), shifted from the Solar System Barycenter
gSource: CODATA 2018 (JPL SSD Astrodynamic Parameters); the engine's fixed value

gm.source: JPL SSD Astrodynamic Parameters, DE440 (Park et al. 2021, AJ 161:105)

radius.source: JPL SSD Planetary Physical Parameters, mean radius (Archinal et al. 2018)

state.note: Horizons geometric state relative to the Solar System Barycenter, km -> m by x1000, before the barycentre shift

gm.source: JPL SSD Astrodynamic Parameters, DE440 (Park et al. 2021, AJ 161:105)

radius.source: JPL SSD planetary satellite physical parameters, mean radius

state.note: Horizons geometric state relative to the Solar System Barycenter, km -> m by x1000, before the barycentre shift

omitted: the Sun and every other body: the solar tide on the Earth-Moon system and on a translunar trajectory is absent (its size is measured in tests/validation/test_spaceflight_validation.py)
assumptions: positions are DE441 vectors, masses are DE440 GM
m = GM / G, so the source GM is reproduced exactly
Earth and Moon states come from Horizons (CENTER=500@0) at the same epoch; removing the barycentre motion leaves their relative state unchanged
limitations: without the Sun the Moon's orbit is a two-body ellipse: its real evection and variation (solar perturbations of the lunar orbit) are absent, so the Moon's position departs from the ephemeris within days
a spacecraft here feels Earth and Moon only: a plan made in this universe is not a prediction for the real Earth-Moon system
history is recorded every 180 s; recording stops when the per-universe cap is reached (about 139 days with three bodies)
